items.title: Correctness
items.question: Does the patch actually do what the task asked, without introducing a wrong result, a crash, or an off-by-one?
items.evidence: Read the changed functions line by line; trace at least one input through the new control flow; check every early return and error branch.

items.title: Spec compliance
items.question: Does the patch satisfy every acceptance criterion in the plan, and none of the forbidden constraints?
items.evidence: Map each acceptance criterion to the lines that satisfy it; name any criterion with no corresponding change.

items.title: Tests
items.question: Are the new or changed behaviors covered by tests that would fail if the change were reverted?
items.evidence: Point at the assertions that pin the new behavior; flag tests that assert only that the code runs.

items.title: No placeholders
items.question: Is the patch free of stubs, TODO markers, commented-out work, and functions that return a canned value?
items.evidence: Quote any added line containing TODO/FIXME/placeholder/not implemented, or any function body that ignores its arguments.

items.title: Scope discipline
items.question: Does the patch touch only what the task needs, with no drive-by reformatting or unrelated refactors?
items.evidence: List changed files that are not in the plan's files_to_touch and say why each is or is not justified.

items.title: Error handling
items.question: Are failures surfaced rather than swallowed, with useful context and no empty catch blocks?
items.evidence: Quote every added catch/except; check that inputs crossing a trust boundary are validated.

items.title: No secrets
items.question: Does the patch add any credential, API key, token, private key, or production endpoint with embedded auth?
items.evidence: Quote any added literal that looks like a key or a token; check test fixtures and config files too.

items.title: Style consistency
items.question: Does the new code match the conventions already used in the files it touches?
items.evidence: Compare imports, naming, error style, and module layout against the surrounding file.

items.title: Reversibility
items.question: Can this change be reverted cleanly, without data migrations, deletions, or irreversible side effects?
items.evidence: Name any destructive operation (schema drop, file delete, network write) and whether it is guarded.
